# Role Fillers Reference

Complete reference for the `glassfrog fillers` command — who fills a role, with each filling's focus and election context.

## Overview

`glassfrog fillers <ROLE_ID>` lists a role's assignments — the actors who fill it — via `GET /roles/{role_id}/assignments`. It is the role-scoped assignment read of the Actor Reads family, distinct from:

- `glassfrog actors` (the actor **directory** — bare actor records for discovery), and
- `glassfrog assignments <ACTOR_ID>` (the same `Assignment` resource read **by actor**).

There is deliberately **no** singular `filler <id>` sibling: the API exposes no `GET /assignments/{id}`, so a single-read command would have no endpoint to call. `fillers` is a single command with one required positional. Paginated — walks every page by default.

Codebase enrichment skipped — not attempted. This reference is based on the interface contracts and the shipped `--help`.

## `glassfrog fillers <ROLE_ID>` — list who fills a role

### Synopsis

```
glassfrog fillers <ROLE_ID> [--first-page] [--per-page N] [--base-url URL] [-o FORMAT]
```

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ROLE_ID` | string | required | The role whose fillers to read (`role_…`). Not validated locally — a malformed or unknown value surfaces as the API's clean `404`. Omitting it, or passing more than one positional, is a usage error before any request (`cobra.ExactArgs(1)`). |

### Flags

There are **no filter flags** — `listRoleAssignments` accepts no query filter beyond pagination, and the request always carries the endpoint's default `include=actor` so each filler's `{id, name, kind}` arrives without a flag.

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--first-page` | bool | false | Fetch only the first page and signal if more exist (see [Completeness signalling](#completeness-signalling)). |
| `--per-page` | int | API max | Page size for the walk. The API owns the valid range. |

### Output

Rendered in the resolved format. Format changes rendering, not fetch depth: the list walks to completion in every format (and `--first-page` limits all formats to one page).

Each row leads with the **filling actor** (the answer to "whom do I contact?") and adds the assignment's governance context — `focus` and `elected_until`.

**`full`** — one block per filler:

```
<per_… | agt_…>  [<kind>]
  Name:           <actor name>
  Focus:          <focus | (none)>
  Elected until:  <elected_until | (not an elected seat)>
```

**`compact`** — one line per filler:

```
<per_… | agt_…>  [<kind>]  <actor name>  — focus: <focus | —>; elected until: <elected_until | —>
```

The actor `id` prefix (`per_`/`agt_`) and the `kind` badge let you tell a person from an agent and carry the id forward into the [Actor read](actors.md). `focus` and `elected_until` are **nullable** and render an explicit-absence marker when unset — never a blank that hides "no focus" / "not an elected seat".

**`json` / `yaml`** — the aggregated `{data:[…]}` document built from each assignment's raw bytes (per-page `meta` dropped). The structured object carries the full assignment (`id`, `actor_id`, `role_id`, `focus`, `elected_until`, embedded `actor`) regardless of the human projection. The assignment's own id (`asgn_…`) appears in structured output but not in the human rows. A valid empty list is `{"data": []}`, never `null`.

**Empty list** (the role has no fillers): under `full`/`compact`, stdout is the `fillers` template's empty line (`no fillers`) and the command exits `0` — an unfilled role is a valid answer, not an error.

## Projection fields

### Assignment (a filler)

| Field | Human projection | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Actor id | row lead | `per_…` (person) or `agt_…` (agent). |
| Kind | `[<kind>]` badge | Person vs agent. |
| Name | `Name:` | The filling actor's name. |
| Focus | `Focus:` | Nullable; `(none)` / `—` when unset. |
| Elected until | `Elected until:` | Nullable; `(not an elected seat)` / `—` when unset. |
| Assignment id | — (structured only) | `asgn_…`; present in `json`/`yaml`, not rendered in human output. |
| `actor_id` / `role_id` / embedded `actor` | — (structured only) | Present in `json`/`yaml`. |

## Completeness signalling

A partial list is never silently presented as complete — signalled via a note on **stderr**.

| Situation | Behaviour | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| Default (full walk) | Walks every page and renders the complete set. | 0 |
| `--first-page`, more pages exist | Renders the first page; writes to stderr: `note: more fillers exist than shown; re-run without --first-page to fetch all` | 0 |
| Mid-walk failure | Renders fillers gathered so far; writes to stderr: `note: result is incomplete — <cause>; the fillers shown are a partial set` | non-zero |

## Output formats

Inherited persistent root flags, read by cobra inheritance:

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--base-url URL` | Override the API base URL (top rung of the base-URL precedence chain). |
| `-o`, `--output FORMAT` | `full` (default), `compact`, `json`, or `yaml` — or, at the flag only, a user-template ref (a template file path, or `stdin`; see [User-Defined Template Output](user-defined-template-output.md)). Resolution chain: flag → `GLASSFROG_OUTPUT` → `.glassfrogrc output` → `full` (env/config accept only the four tokens). |

The raw API envelope is never emitted under a human format.

## Failure rendering

Failure rendering is **format-aware** (Output-Aware Failure Rendering): under `json`/`yaml` a failure emits the unified error envelope on **stdout**; under `full`/`compact` the diagnostic (cause + next step) goes to **stderr**. The incompleteness notes stay on **stderr** in every format.

## Exit codes and errors

The exit code is the category from the Exit-Code Convention. Every message names the cause and a next step, and never includes the token.

| Condition | Exit | Diagnostic |
|---|---|---|
| Fillers listed (incl. empty list) | 0 | — (result on stdout; incompleteness note on stderr when applicable) |
| No usable token | 2 | "not authenticated — run `glassfrog auth login` or set GLASSFROG_TOKEN" |
| Unreadable / malformed credential file | 1 | names the credentials file — "fix or re-create it with `glassfrog auth login`" |
| Unknown or malformed role id, or other non-2xx (4xx/5xx) | 3 / 4 / 5 | names the HTTP status + extracted detail; per-class next step (an unknown role id is typically `404`) |
| Could not reach the wire | 6 | names the transport failure — "check connectivity; the API may be unreachable" |
| 2xx body did not match the expected shape | 3 | "the API response did not match the expected shape — may be an API change; report it" |
| Malformed paging mid-walk | 1 | the walker's text, surfaced inside the incompleteness note |
| Base-URL configuration error | 2 | names the malformed base URL + source |
| Invalid `--output` selector | 2 | names the bad format value + the four valid names |
| Missing or extra positional, or unknown flag | 2 | cobra's `ExactArgs(1)` / unknown-flag message; no request sent |

Exit codes by category: `0` success, `1` runtime error, `2` usage error, `3` API error, `4` permission error, `5` rate-limited, `6` network unavailable.
